channel.title: The Thinking Dojo: articles for parents and teachers
channel.description: Short, practical articles on helping children aged 7 to 13 think for themselves.

item.title: Three questions for Anti-Bullying Week: notice, choose, act
item.description: Anti-Bullying Week 2026 runs from 16 to 20 November with the theme Break the Silence. Three five-minute questions that help children aged 7 to 13 notice, choose and act.

item.title: How do I teach my child to think for themselves?
item.description: Thinking for yourself is seven smaller skills that build in order. Here is the order, with one question for each that you can ask at home tonight.

item.title: What to ask instead of “How was school?”
item.description: “Fine” is an honest answer to a vague question. Two better questions that get a child describing their day, and how to ask them.

item.title: My child rushes and makes careless mistakes. What helps?
item.description: Telling a child to slow down rarely works. Helping them spot their own pattern does. Two questions to try, and when to ask them.

item.title: How to help your child make decisions
item.description: Children get better at deciding by practising on small choices. Two questions that slow a decision down without making it for them.

item.title: What to say to your child after a bad result
item.description: After a lost match or a poor test, when you ask matters as much as what you ask. A simple order to follow, and one question that turns it into learning.

item.title: Seven screen-free thinking activities for children aged 7 to 13
item.description: Seven short activities that need no screen, no worksheet and no preparation. One for each thinking skill, from noticing to thinking independently.

item.title: Five-minute thinking starters for the classroom
item.description: A week of five-minute thinking starters for ages 7 to 13, built around planning, doing and reviewing. All you need is one question on the board.

item.title: A simple thinking-skills routine for home education
item.description: How to add thinking skills to a home-education week in about ten minutes a day, without another curriculum to manage.
